11: /// ## What it does
12: /// Checks for negated `==` operators.
13: ///
14: /// ## Why is this bad?
15: /// Negated `==` operators are less readable than `!=` operators. When testing
16: /// for non-equality, it is more common to use `!=` than `==`.
17: ///
18: /// ## Example
19: /// ```python
20: /// not a == b
21: /// ```
22: ///
23: /// Use instead:
24: /// ```python
25: /// a != b
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## References
29: /// - [Python documentation: Comparisons](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#comparisons)
30: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
31: pub(crate) struct NegateEqualOp {
32:     left: String,
33:     right: String,
34: }
35: 
36: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for NegateEqualOp {
37:     #[derive_message_formats]
38:     fn message(&self) -> String {
39:         let NegateEqualOp { left, right } = self;
40:         format!("Use `{left} != {right}` instead of `not {left} == {right}`")
41:     }
42: 
43:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
44:         "Replace with `!=` operator".to_string()
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: /// ## What it does
49: /// Checks for negated `!=` operators.
50: ///
51: /// ## Why is this bad?
52: /// Negated `!=` operators are less readable than `==` operators, as they avoid a
53: /// double negation.
54: ///
55: /// ## Example
56: /// ```python
57: /// not a != b
58: /// ```
59: ///
60: /// Use instead:
61: /// ```python
62: /// a == b
63: /// ```
64: ///
65: /// ## References
66: /// - [Python documentation: Comparisons](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#comparisons)
67: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
68: pub(crate) struct NegateNotEqualOp {
69:     left: String,
70:     right: String,
71: }
72: 
73: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for NegateNotEqualOp {
74:     #[derive_message_formats]
75:     fn message(&self) -> String {
76:         let NegateNotEqualOp { left, right } = self;
77:         format!("Use `{left} == {right}` instead of `not {left} != {right}`")
78:     }
79: 
80:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
81:         "Replace with `==` operator".to_string()
82:     }
83: }

85: /// ## What it does
86: /// Checks for double negations (i.e., multiple `not` operators).
87: ///
88: /// ## Why is this bad?
89: /// A double negation is redundant and less readable than omitting the `not`
90: /// operators entirely.
91: ///
92: /// ## Example
93: /// ```python
94: /// not (not a)
95: /// ```
96: ///
97: /// Use instead:
98: /// ```python
99: /// a
100: /// ```
101: ///
102: /// ## References
103: /// - [Python documentation: Comparisons](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#comparisons)
104: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
105: pub(crate) struct DoubleNegation {
106:     expr: String,
107: }
108: 
109: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for DoubleNegation {
110:     #[derive_message_formats]
111:     fn message(&self) -> String {
112:         let DoubleNegation { expr } = self;
113:         format!("Use `{expr}` instead of `not (not {expr})`")
114:     }
115: 
116:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
117:         let DoubleNegation { expr } = self;
118:         format!("Replace with `{expr}`")
119:     }
120: }

122: fn is_dunder_method(name: &str) -> bool {
123:     matches!(

137: pub(crate) fn negation_with_equal_op(
138:     checker: &mut Checker,
139:     expr: &Expr,

142: ) {

145:     }

147:         left,
148:         ops,

154:     };

157:     }

159:         return;
160:     }

163:     if let ScopeKind::Function(ast::StmtFunctionDef { name, .. }) =
164:         &checker.semantic().current_scope().kind
165:     {
166:         if is_dunder_method(name) {
167:             return;
168:         }
169:     }
170: 
171:     let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(
172:         NegateEqualOp {
173:             left: checker.generator().expr(left),
174:             right: checker.generator().expr(&comparators[0]),
175:         },
176:         expr.range(),
177:     );
178:     let node = ast::ExprCompare {
179:         left: left.clone(),
180:         ops: Box::from([CmpOp::NotEq]),
181:         comparators: comparators.clone(),
182:         range: TextRange::default(),
183:     };
184:     diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::safe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
185:         checker.generator().expr(&node.into()),
186:         expr.range(),
187:     )));
188:     checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
189: }

228:             left: checker.generator().expr(left),
229:             right: checker.generator().expr(&comparators[0]),
230:         },
231:         expr.range(),

233:     let node = ast::ExprCompare {
234:         left: left.clone(),
235:         ops: Box::from([CmpOp::Eq]),
236:         comparators: comparators.clone(),
237:         range: TextRange::default(),
238:     };
239:     diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::safe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(

243:     checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);

247: pub(crate) fn double_negation(checker: &mut Checker, expr: &Expr, op: UnaryOp, operand: &Expr) {
248:     if !matches!(op, UnaryOp::Not) {
249:         return;
250:     }
251:     let Expr::UnaryOp(ast::ExprUnaryOp {
252:         op: operand_op,
253:         operand,
254:         range: _,
255:     }) = operand
256:     else {
257:         return;
258:     };
259:     if !matches!(operand_op, UnaryOp::Not) {
260:         return;
261:     }
262: 
263:     let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(
264:         DoubleNegation {
265:             expr: checker.generator().expr(operand),
266:         },
267:         expr.range(),
268:     );
269:     if checker.semantic().in_boolean_test() {
270:         diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::safe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
271:             checker.locator().slice(operand.as_ref()).to_string(),
272:             expr.range(),
273:         )));
274:     } else if checker.semantic().has_builtin_binding("bool") {
275:         let node = ast::ExprName {
276:             id: Name::new_static("bool"),
277:             ctx: ExprContext::Load,
278:             range: TextRange::default(),
